matched.title: User authorization does not bind fee_amount or fee_recipient, so the submitter chooses where the fee goes

findings.title: User authorization does not bind fee_amount or fee_recipient, so the submitter chooses where the fee goes
User signature does not bind fee_recipient or fee_amount, so the submitter can redirect the fee
Soroban contract arithmetic can wrap around in release builds
Allowlist entries are written to persistent storage with no TTL extension at write time, and the removal path panics if an entry has expired
Removing the last allowed fee token silently turns the allowlist off and accepts any token
Public helpers collect_fee, sweep_token and set_allowed_fee_token perform no authorization, and integrators must add it

failing_checks.title: Recipient binding
failing_checks.reason: fee_recipient is a plain function argument. It is not in the signed user_args_for_auth tuple (storage.rs:90-98), and no allowlist or operator binding checks it. The submitter chooses where the user's fee goes. This is the defect already recorded as intent-ai-intent-mismatch-1.
